Ordinary Time July 26 2026 This weekend July 25th 26th the Church celebrates the Seventeenth Sunday in Ordinary Time Our Gospel reading brings an end to the Parabolic Discourse within St Matthew's Gospel that began two weeks ago Following the four public parables shared to this point we now hear in quick succession the last three private parables The public parables were shared with the large crowds the private parables only with the disciples All three of these private parables of the kingdom the treasure hidden in a field the pearl of great price and the net that gathers fish of every kind all ask the same question What is the Kingdom truly worth Jesus invites us to see that the Kingdom is worth more than anything else we could ever possess Those who recognize its value will gladly surrender everything to obtain it This same theme runs through every reading today Solomons wisdom 1 Kings 35 7 12 the Psalmists delight Psalm 119 and Pauls confidence remind us that God alone is the treasure worth everything Romans 828 30 Everything else eventually passes away but the Kingdom of God endures forever May we have hearts wise enough to recognize its incomparable worth Liturgical Arrangements General Updates With the ongoing flooring work in the Sanctuary we are unable to open the dust screen into the construction zone and extend our makeshift sanctuary As such weve shifted our liturgical arrangements from using the versus populum altar style to the ad orientem style This change greatly shrinks the footprint for our make shift sanctuary and keeps a safe amount of space between the altar and front pew for the distribution of Holy Communion As the flooring work continues we are asking that you do not open and peek your head behind the dust screen into the construction zone after Masses or during the day As fun as it has been to sneak peeks at the progress our flooring crew will have tiles placed all around the sanctuary for the next two three weeks As such they have asked that no one opens the construction zone as a safety precaution both for ourselves and the loose tile On Friday we had our latest progress meeting with Shawnee Construction As of our meeting they are still confident of nearing completion the last week of August Their goal at this time is to complete as much as possible so that our sanctuary can be reopened and used for our weekend Masses Once the sanctuary is fully reopen for weekends the construction team will continue to work on any remaining fixes throughout the weeks This will also include the stencil work to be completed in the Church which will most likely be scheduled in the coming months to best work with the artist's schedule Time Away in August and Welcoming Fr Theodore As you may recall I am completing a longstanding thesis for my licentiate through Catholic University of America I had previously requested an opportunity to take leave from the parish to complete this work and have now received permission from the diocese to do so This means that I will be away from the parish from August 8th 23rd to work with my advisor on completing my thesis regarding parish registration in the United States This leave is possible because the diocese is assigning Fr Theodore Ekwem to our parish throughout these two weeks Fr Theodore is a priest of the Diocese of Ekwulobia in southeast Nigeria assisting in our diocese at various parishes through November In November he will serve as an observer at our diocesan synod before then returning to his home diocese Thank you for the warm welcome you will show Fr Theodore in the coming weeks Given the great difficulty in arranging this leave my last day away from the parish was December 26 2025 I want to maximize the time that I will have for writing This means that throughout these two weeks I will be off campus and completely unreachable For any needs or concerns that may arise please contact the Parish Office Fr Theodore will be staying on campus at the
